caption: This could be why your baby isn’t eating what you want them to eat, especially veggies … There are a handful of common reasons babies refuse food. Here are six I see most often: 1️⃣ They’re tired: Learning to eat takes coordination and focus. If your baby is exhausted, they may not have the energy to engage with food. ➡️ Try offering meals when your baby is well-rested and hungry! Like right after a nap. 2️⃣ They’re not feeling well: Appetite often drops when babies are sick or coming down with something. This is completely normal. ➡️ During illness, prioritize fluids and milk feeds. Once they’re feeling better, their appetite typically comes back. Stick with familiar foods and give it time. 3️⃣ Teething discomfort: Sore gums can make eating less appealing. ➡️ Offer soothing, cool foods like yogurt, cucumber, or chilled fruit. A cold teether before meals can also help reduce discomfort. You can also try offering frozen veggies to gnaw on! 4️⃣ Not hungry enough: If your baby isn’t showing interest, they might not be hungry enough, so they’re less motivated to try new foods. ➡️ Adjust timing of breastmilk or bottle feeds so they come to the table ready (but not desperate) to eat. 5️⃣ They want independence: Many babies prefer to take the lead with feeding and may resist being spoon-fed. ➡️ Let them explore by feeding themselves. You can hand them pieces of food or offer a preloaded spoon to support independence. 6️⃣ They’re still learning: Eating is a brand new skill, and some babies simply aren’t sure what to do yet. ➡️ One of the most effective ways to teach is by modeling. Let your baby watch you eat and eat with you, they learn a lot just by observing. Notice how none of these reasons has anything to do with your baby not liking the veggie or food you’re trying to serve them! Picky eating is often about a variety of things, not just the food. Which means that small adjustments to timing, environment, and approach can make a big difference over time!  If your baby isn’t eating, you’re not alone. Don’t give up and keep giving them the foods you want them to eat!   Follow for more daily feeding tips. #pickyeating #pickyeater
